problem: Prior open-vocabulary mobile manipulation (OVMM) systems refresh their 3D semantic world representation only at discrete milestones (navigation targets, sub-action ends) because semantic 3D reconstruction is slow. Robots therefore miss objects en route, detect errors late, and replan slowly.
motivation: Real homes and offices change during execution (objects and receptacles move). Robots must either pause often for expensive reconstruction or move with stale information. The paper observes that monitoring needs only lightweight semantic awareness, while planning needs precise geometry, so the two can be split.
key_idea: A dual-process (System 1 / System 2) framework: a Video-LLM (IRM) continuously monitors the video stream and triggers continue/adjust/replan, while a multimodal LLM (DRM) does deliberate planning on 3D voxel-map reconstruction and gives the IRM task-specific guidance.
insight: Continuous video monitoring recovers most of the missed-change failures without stopping for reconstruction, and DRM guidance makes the monitoring task-aware. In the Task 3 ablation, Neither gives SR 0.30, DRM only 0.40, IRM only 0.60 and DRM+IRM 0.80. DRM mainly improves SPL (0.22 to 0.38) and the IRM mainly improves SR/PSR. The tabletop study shows IRM lifts SR from 0.53 to 0.77 for only about 5 s extra.
method: Dual-process architecture: decouples continuous semantic monitoring (IRM, System 1) from costly periodic 3D reconstruction and planning (DRM, System 2).

DRM: GPT-5 takes the instruction P and memory M_t (DynaMem 3D voxel map, 2D occupancy, action history, object registry). It outputs the next action (go_to/explore/grasp/place), a target, and a guidance prompt G for the IRM. It runs at navigation targets or when the IRM triggers it, after a look_around reconstruction.

IRM: Qwen2.5-VL-3B processes 1 s clips at 8 fps (about 0.5 s inference, about 12 GB VRAM) with guidance G and produces text reports Z_t. A guidance-conditioned parser (MPNet embedding matching) extracts detected objects and an execution mode in {continue, adjust, replan}.
Asynchronous localization: matched objects are boxed with OWL-ViT and lifted to 3D by the median of RGB-D projected points. They are merged into the object registry without stopping the robot.

DRM top-k frontier selection: DynaMem value V=V^T+V^S ranks frontiers. Spatially diverse k=3 candidates are chosen, the camera is turned toward each, and the DRM picks the most promising view. A* then plans the path.

Manipulation: built on OK-Robot (AnyGrasp + LangSAM). On adjust, AnyGrasp recomputes grasps locally, or placement height or receptacle is changed. On replan, the DRM re-reconstructs and revises the plan.
Bidirectional coordination: the DRM's guidance retargets the IRM's attention (search vs. gripper alignment). The IRM updates the registry and escalates to the DRM only when needed.

setting.backbone: GPT-5 (DRM, frozen) + Qwen2.5-VL-3B (IRM Video-LLM, frozen) with CLIP, OWL-ViT, MPNet, AnyGrasp, LangSAM
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (head RealSense D435i, wrist D405) plus continuous video stream
setting.action_space: high-level primitives (go_to, explore, grasp, place) executed by A* navigation and AnyGrasp/IK manipulation
setting.privileged: none (baselines OK-Robot and DovSG use pre-scanned maps, best of five scans)

numbers.eval_set_note: 40 trials, real-world office with object/receptacle perturbations
numbers.extra: real-world Stretch SE3; dynamic perturbations during execution

40 trials, three objects to three receptacles

numbers_note: All benchmarks are the authors' own real-world setups, not standard benchmarks. Ablation (Task 3, office, 10 trials): DRM+IRM SR 0.80, PSR 0.93, SPL 0.63, PSPL 0.82. Tabletop manipulation (30 trials): SR 0.77, 66 s. Task 3 office: 21.90 min, 28.35 m vs DynaMem 33.83 min, 39.60 m.
results: BINDER beats the strongest baseline DynaMem in the office: SR 0.93 vs 0.60 (Task 1), 0.78 vs 0.43 (Task 2), 0.63 vs 0.15 (Task 3). In homes it reaches SR 0.70 (studio) and 0.80 (3-room) vs DynaMem 0.30 and 0.50. It is also faster and shorter than DynaMem on Task 3 (21.90 vs 33.83 min; 28.35 vs 39.60 m).
limitations: Evaluated only on a small number of real-world trials (10-40 per setting) on one robot platform, with no standard benchmark or simulation. Perturbations are hand-designed.
Remaining failures are fine-grained: collisions, misaligned placement, undetected objects and grasp failures. Some navigation failures were manual collision-risk stops.
Relies on GPT-5 through an external workstation over Wi-Fi, and the baselines were adapted to multi-object tasks by running them sequentially.
